title: Bulk report - Week 42
summary:
Capesize
The market endured a sustained and broad-based decline through the week, with the BCI 182 5TC falling from $37,618 at Monday's close to $29,464 by Friday. Persistent selling pressure across both basins drove rates lower, with sentiment deteriorating as the week progressed. The Pacific remained under pressure throughout, with limited miner participation and insufficient fresh enquiry to support rates.

children.title: Panamax-Kamsarmax
children.summary: The week opened with a largely balanced Atlantic market, where a steady flow of mineral cargoes supported transatlantic activity, although sufficient vessel availability continued to limit any meaningful upside. A 75,000-dwt vessel was reported fixed for a US Gulf transatlantic trip at $21,500.

children.title: Ultramax/Supramax
children.summary: The index saw slow gains throughout the week driven mainly by the Asian market. The US Gulf started on a steady footing with a 63,000-dwt fixed US Gulf to China with petcoke at $34,000, but rates later softened as surplus tonnage took effect.

children.title: Handysize
children.summary: The Handysize market delivered a mixed performance across the regions this week. The Continent and Mediterranean remained stable, supported by a healthy cargo book.
